name: Place Attachment Theory
citation: Scannell, L. & Gifford, R. (2010). Defining place attachment: A tripartite organizing framework. J. Environ. Psychol., 30(1), 1-10.

constructs.description: Events become autobiographically tied to spatial context via hippocampal place cell reinstatement during retrieval.
Body's allostatic calibration built over years of habituation to specific spatial, thermal, acoustic, and social patterns.
Forced relocation produces massive interoceptive disruption — body-budget crisis (IC) + hippocampal reinstatement failure + SN disorientation.
IE-DPT requires temporal extension: explicit evaluations over months/years sediment into implicit embodied security. Novel meta-template requirement.

schema_gaps: Biographical Explicit Integration meta-template not yet implemented
Olfactory and proprioceptive channels of place memory untemplate
irreducible_residual.narrative: Largest irreducible residual (~40%) of any formal T1.5 reduction. Cultural specification of attachment objects (~15%), social-relational attachment where community bonds are load-bearing (~15%), and narrative/cultural heritage attachment (~10%). People are often attached to COMMUNITIES IN PLACES more than to physical places themselves, and this social dimension resists neural-architectural reduction.

key_references: Scannell, L. & Gifford, R. (2010). J. Environ. Psychol., 30(1), 1-10.

boundary_criteria.boundary_justification: PLACE_ATTACHMENT has irreducible person-place bonds (compositional_adequacy = EMERGENT_RESIDUAL with 40% residual including cultural attachment objects, social bonds, narrative heritage). Design guidance is actionable: designing for place identity, heritage preservation, community gathering spaces produces measurable attachment and reduces displacement grief. However, constitutive_relevance is FALSE: mechanism is underspecified. The theory names 'place attachment' but does not identify the constitutively relevant intervening variable — is it episodic memory, allostatic calibration, social bonds, or narrative identity? Without mechanism specificity, interventions are weak.

function_form.function_form: PA(p, ψ, t) = [PD(p,ψ), PI(p,ψ)] · log(1 + t/τ); τ ≈ 2 years
predictions: Place attachment grows logarithmically (rapid early, plateau ~5 years)
Involuntary displacement causes grief proportional to PA strength

provenance.foundational_paper: Altman, I., & Low, S.M. (Eds.). (1992). Place Attachment. New York: Plenum Press.
provenance.modern_synthesis: Scannell, L., & Gifford, R. (2010). Defining place attachment: A tripartite organizing framework. Journal of Environmental Psychology, 30(1), 1-10. doi:10.1016/j.jenvp.2009.06.002
provenance.predecessor: Environmental psychology tradition; Tuan's topophilia concept (1974); human-environment interaction research
provenance.historical_context: Irwin Altman and Setha M. Low edited landmark 1992 volume establishing place attachment as multidisciplinary concept. Brown and Perkins (in Altman & Low) synthesized prior work, defining place attachments as positively experienced bonds individuals and groups form with sociophysical environments, involving behavioral, cognitive, and affective ties. Later, Scannell & Gifford (2010) provided tripartite organizing framework: person dimension (individuals, families, communities), process dimension (cognitive, emotional, social bonds), and place dimension (specific locations, neighborhoods, communities). Volume integrated environmental psychology, geography, urban planning, social psychology, and anthropology.
key_milestones: 1970s-1980s: Emerging research on human-place bonds and identity
1992: Altman & Low landmark edited volume establishing comprehensive framework
1990s-2000s: Extensive empirical research on attachment across place types
2010: Scannell & Gifford tripartite framework synthesis and organizational model
2000s-Present: Applications to heritage conservation, urban planning, relocation research
influenced_by: Irwin Altman (environmental psychologist, place and privacy)
Setha M. Low (anthropologist, place and culture)
David Brown & Penny Perkins (empirical validation framework)
provenance.current_status: foundational and actively researched across environmental psychology, anthropology, and urban planning

Scannell & Gifford (2010) modern synthesis verified via Journal of Environmental Psychology.
